set.approach: The ice forms on the open cliff band west of Mary's Lake, above Joe's Valley Reservoir. In a lean snow year or early in the season a vehicle can reach the lake area; later the road is usually covered, and a ski or snowmobile approach works better. From the south end of the reservoir the road continues south, then turns back north toward the lake. From the lake, or the forest south of it, head west through the trees to the cliff band and make a beeline for the flows, which are visible from below when they have formed. It is a short walk from the lake. Alzcleimbers is the stepped line immediately right of Dirty Blonde.

review.notes: Approach from the Lake Mary Ice area page; position from the route page. No descent stated.

set.descent_text: After the steep ice, a short bowl angles up and to the right to a tree. Get down by rappelling from that tree, and bring cord or webbing to build the anchor.

set.descent_text: The ice eases to thin, low-angle ground below the trees at the top. Rappel from a tree there.

set.descent_text: After pulling over the lip of the vertical pillar the ice ends and a short stretch of easy mixed ground leads to a chain anchor on the right, which can be buried in snow, or to a fixed anchor higher and to the left.
set.approach: Park at the White Pine lot in Little Cottonwood Canyon, cross the road to the north side and walk up the south-facing Little Pine chute until you see the ice at the foot of the Jedediah chute. Skiers use the chute, so keep an eye uphill, and check the avalanche forecast since the whole drainage lies in avalanche paths.

review.notes: Approach from the Limber Pine Ice area page; the parent page confirms the White Pine trailhead and the Jedediah path. Top-out from the route page.

set.descent_text: Three ways down from the top of the climbing. Rappel from the fixed anchor to the snowfield above the thickest ice, walk right and rappel again from a good tree, or traverse the large ledge to the north and descend the prominent couloir.
set.approach: Park at the Highline lot on the Mirror Lake Highway and head north beneath Hayden Peak. The efficient line keeps to the trees right at the edge of the talus field; skis make the walk much easier when there is snow. The route starts a few hundred metres right of the prominent couloir on the far lower left side of the peak. The highway is seasonal and closes for the winter, so the route is best early in the season; check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Approach from area page and route page; route is on the far lower left of Hayden Peak. Descent options from the route page only; the AAC write-up says the first ascent party walked off the talus above.

set.approach: From the Middle Fork Weber River trailhead follow the trail on foot or skis to the sign for the Abes Lake turn-off. Leave the trail shortly after the sign and keep the river on your left as you work upstream along its bank to the falls, then drop below them to the base. Check that the ice is sound as you approach, because a deep pool sits at the foot of the falls.

review.notes: Trailhead, sign and route position from the area page and the route page (both say about three miles; count left out).

ut_middle_fork_weber_river_ice_2_temptat.skip_reason: ice bouldering, out of scope (the route page itself calls it ice bouldering)

set.descent_text: From the top of the ice continue up a few rock steps on the climber's left to a group of trees and rappel from them. A rappel down the quartzite slab drops into a small couloir that leads back to your packs.
set.approach: Park in the Gad Valley lot at Snowbird, cross the road into a stand of aspens and climb the open south-facing slope, then trend right toward the East Gully of Monte Cristo. The route starts a little below the ridge crest in the East Gully, on the climber's right of the top. It is visible from the canyon road. Check the avalanche forecast, since the slope is steep open ground.

review.notes: Single route page gives approach and descent; this route is in Little Cottonwood Canyon at Alta, not at the row's stored coordinates (Timpanogos).

set.approach: Park at the Highline trailhead and take the trail toward Naturalist Basin. The ice flows down northwest-aspect couloirs on the west side of the cirque below Mount Agassiz's summit. A big stretch of burned forest is the cue to leave the trail to the left and climb to the ice. Courduroy Cascade is the second couloir, a couple of hundred feet right of Training Wheels.

review.notes: Approach from area page; position from route page.

set.descent_text: Walk off down the left-hand branch of the same couloir.
set.approach: Park at the Highline trailhead and take the trail toward Naturalist Basin. The ice flows down northwest-aspect couloirs on the west side of the cirque below Mount Agassiz's summit. A big stretch of burned forest is the cue to leave the trail to the left and climb to the ice. Go to the left-most couloir, which splits into two forks; Training Wheels sits in the right-hand branch and stays hidden until you are right below it.

review.notes: Approach from area page; position and walk-off from route page.

set.descent_text: After the roped pitches the party unropes and scrambles third-class and gully ground to the summit. From there, follow the hiking trail down, or use one of the ski race start chutes.
set.approach: Start from the Snowbasin base area; the Needles gondola, when it is running, shortens the walk. From the top station skirt below the Needles and walk to the low point of the Gray Slabs on the south end of the northeast face of Mt. Ogden. The Southeast Ridge begins at the obvious feature just around the corner to the left of where the Gray Slabs start.

review.notes: Position from the route page; approach to the Gray Slabs end of the face from the Mt. Ogden and Snowbasin area pages (one lineage). Descent from the route page only.

set.descent_text: From the top of the couloir there are several ways down. Descend the northwest ridge to a dirt road and walk it back to the car, glissade the neighbouring Cold Fusion couloir if it holds snow, or continue along the summit ridge to the main summit first.
set.approach: Start from the Timpooneke trailhead in American Fork Canyon (in winter, from the Mutual Dell campground when the road is closed). Climb into the Wooly Hole cirque and contour right and up a broad face to the foot of the couloir, which is that divides into a pair of branches. A helmet matters because the couloir sheds rock, and check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Approach: route page and a ski-objective page agree on the trailhead and Wooly Hole cirque. Descent options from the route page.

set.approach: From the Aspen Grove trailhead follow the trail up into the Lost Lake cirque. Where the trail turns north, a weakness in the cliff band may hold a thin WI3 smear or be filled with snow that makes an approach ramp. If it is dry, continue on the trail to Emerald Lake, turn left at the rock bridge on the unmaintained trail onto the plateau above the cirque, and pick a line across the talus to the foot of the ramp under the climbs. The approach is long, and rockfall is a hazard on the talus. Moist and Juicy is the thin line in the left-facing corner on the shoulder under the south summit.

review.notes: Approach from the route page. No descent stated.

set.approach: Start from the Aspen Grove trailhead, a couple of miles past the Sundance turn-off up Provo Canyon, and walk a short way up the Timpanogos trail to the second waterfall. The ice forms early because the spot is shaded.

review.notes: Approach from the route page. No descent stated (the page describes top-rope anchors in bushes above).

set.descent_text: A rappel station sits on the trees to the climber's right on the ledge above the climb. Loose rock litters the ledge and the cliffs around it, so protect the belayer and rappel with care.

review.notes: Approach from the Twin Daggers and Moist and Juicy pages (the first points to the second); descent from the Twin Daggers page.

set.approach: Nordic ski from North Fork Park to the base of Coldwater Falls, finishing with a short boot-pack. The climb follows the creek, with several short ice steps separated by snow bridges and frozen creek crossings, and it does not form every winter. Check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Approach from the route page only; no descent stated.

set.approach: The way in starts at the Trail Lake trailhead, passes Wall Lake and crosses the Notch. Descend the trail toward Ibantik Lake, but break right across talus before you reach the water and contour under Notch Mountain's north face. The ice lines are gullies on the northeast buttress, counted from the climber's right as you traverse in along the base of the wall. Axe of Desperation is the third narrow ice gully, with a small roof about fifty feet up just after a squeeze chimney.

review.notes: Approach from area page; position from route page. No descent stated.

set.descent_text: From the top of the ice, traverse right to a piton anchor and lower off. A second pitch was not found to have good anchors, so the first ascent party downclimbed to the first anchor.

set.descent_text: There is no tree to thread, so a rappel from the top of the ice lands in snow that you downclimb. Carry a few pitons in case the upper ice is too thin to build a rappel anchor.

set.descent_text: From the ridge at the top of the climb, head to the climber's right and descend the talus, which is slow and awkward when it is snow-covered, down to the trail and out.

review.notes: Descent: route page says go climber's right on the ridge; the AAC write-up agrees the way down is over snow-covered talus to the trail. No approach written: no source names the trailhead or the line to the face.

set.approach: The black Portal Wall sits above a talus slope beside the road a few miles beyond the winter gate. Portal #6 is the last recessed section near the end of the wall; look for it behind pine trees high above the road before the Cobblerest area. The ice is a corner, with additional ice sometimes forming on the main wall.

review.notes: Location from area and route pages. No descent stated.

set.descent_text: Scramble down the opposite side of the ridge and angle left to pick up the usual descent from the Bald Mountain and Reids Peak saddle, which returns down the northeast slope to the base of the routes.
set.approach: The trailhead is Pass Lake. The trail leaving the loop road loops far around to the peak's right-hand side and only then turns back left beneath the north face, so leave it early and head directly uphill to the notch separating Reids Peak from Bald Mountain. The ice and mixed lines are on the north and northeast side of that notch. The routes can also be approached from the shoulder pullout on Highway 150 just north of the Mirror Lake campground entrance. The area is within a national forest fee area. 98 Pounds sits in a small alcove off to the left of both Golden Spike and The One Who Knocks.

review.notes: Approach from area page; position and top-out/descent from the route page, the saddle descent confirmed on Higher Grounds.

set.descent_text: Downclimb the third and fourth-class southeast ridge as far as the head of Scum Couloir, keep following the ridge-side descent line to the Reids-Bald saddle, then drop the northeast slope to the base of the routes.

set.descent_text: Step over the ridge onto its southwest side and traverse southeast to the Reids-Bald saddle. From the saddle go down the northeast slope to the foot of the routes.

set.descent_text: Rappel from trees and a block to the climber's left of the route until you are on the snow shoulder level with the ridge where the other routes top out. Traverse left across the snow to the top of those routes and follow their descent.

set.descent_text: The last pitch is a scramble through mixed steps and a snowy couloir to the ridgeline. From there descend to the col on the climber's left and walk back to the base of the route.

The trail leaving the loop road loops far around to the peak's right-hand side and only then turns back left beneath the north face, so leave it early and head directly uphill to the notch separating Reids Peak from Bald Mountain. set.approach: One option is the big pullout opposite the Storm Mountain picnic area, then a walk through the picnic ground, which is closed in winter. The better option is the pullout on the far side of the road just beyond the bridge, a short drive up-canyon, followed by a walk west along the foot of the cliffs. Glass Case of Emotion begins at the second-pitch anchors of the main Storm Mountain falls, then breaks left up a thin sheet of ice beside the overhanging formation.

review.notes: Approach from area page; this is a variation to Storm Mountain's route after its second pitch. No descent stated.

set.descent_text: Rappel from the fixed anchor at the top; backing it up with a piton is wise.
set.approach: One option is the big pullout opposite the Storm Mountain picnic area, then a walk through the picnic ground, which is closed in winter. PsychoBabble Gully starts at the very back of the west gully used to reach the PsychoBabble wall.

review.notes: Approach from area page; start and anchor from route page.

set.descent_text: The usual way off is to climb the top pillar, go over the top, and descend the gully just east of the ice. If the ice is poor, rappel the route, building V-threads.
set.approach: One option is the big pullout opposite the Storm Mountain picnic area, then a walk through the picnic ground, which is closed in winter. Storm Mountain faces south, just north of the picnic area and east of the PsychoBabble wall.

review.notes: Approach from area page; position and descent from route page.

set.descent_text: From the top of the ice hike a short way north to a gully you can slide down, then walk back to the base.
set.approach: Park above Sundance Resort and hike west toward the gate of the private community. Cross the creek and climb a short slope to find the trail on the north side of the drainage, then continue west along the snowshoe trail to the base of the falls. It is under an hour's walk, and the face gets morning sun.

review.notes: Approach and descent from route page; approach confirmed by area page (same lineage).
